subtype: Approach: setting small goals such as ten metres, then twenty [Revision]
passage: Nilesh could ride only a few metres before his legs stopped and his feet dropped. Every day the same. "I'm not getting anywhere," he told Rajni, kicking the tyre. "Maybe you are," said Rajni. "You never measured." That evening Nilesh took chalk and drew a line at ten metres, another at twenty. The next day he reached the first line on his second try. The day after, he passed it easily and fell just before the second line. He rubbed his knee, but he was grinning, because he could now see that each attempt took him further than the last.

qa.q: What did Nilesh draw on the ground?
qa.a: Nilesh drew a line at ten metres and another at twenty.

qa.q: What did Nilesh feel when he told Rajni he was not getting anywhere?
qa.a: Nilesh felt stuck and discouraged, which is why he kicked the tyre.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Nilesh try, and why?
qa.a: Nilesh could ask an older rider to watch and point out one thing to fix. A fresh pair of eyes can spot problems that are hard to feel.

qa.q: How might Rajni see the chalk lines?
qa.a: Rajni might be pleased that the remark about never measuring turned into real marks on the ground that Nilesh now rides toward.

grounding: Feeling stuck at a few metres, a boy chalks ten- and twenty-metre marks so counting improvement shows him he is getting better despite falls.
